correctness.rationale: For V_d={0,1}^d and S_d=V_d plus all Euclidean edge midpoints, d=2,3, averaging arbitrary signed right-inverse extensions over cube isometries preserves norm and yields stabilizer-orbit coefficients (a,b) or (a,b,c). In d=2 two exact 1-Lipschitz distance potentials give opposite affine lower bounds meeting at b_2; in d=3 f_+=||v|| and the verified non-distance 1-Lipschitz f_- force c-independent bound, which meets the far-midpoint lower bound at b_3. The explicit positive coefficients a=1/2-(d-1)b, b on mismatch-one, zero on mismatch-two in d3 yield probability measures. The finite Kantorovich–Rubinstein dual implies operator norm equals max over 28/190 point pairs of W1(mu_x,mu_y)/||x-y||. The written exact transport couplings cover all vertex and midpoint orbit types (including perpendicular mismatched cube midpoints), yielding matching upper bounds. A separate SciPy LP formulation of all 218 transportation problems recovered both radicals 1.0550500132 and 1.0719126700; the 3D dual potential also passed all 28 vertex-pair Lipschitz inequalities. Finite LP supports, but does not replace, exact symmetry/dual/coupling reasoning.
